newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE suspends BTP December 1997 delivery month.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE suspends BTP December 1997 delivery month.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Tuesday it had suspended the December 1997 delivery month of its Italian government bond (BTP) futures contract, with immediate effect.

"Movements in yields on Italian bond products, in particular in relation to the effects of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) on the contract, have led LIFFE to closely evaluate the implication of changes in the underlying cash markets," the exchange said in a statement.
There is no open interest in the December delivery month, LIFFE said.
June and September contracts are not affected, it added.

"What has happened is that the yields on the Italian bond contract in the cash market have become much lower, therefore we need to review our contract specification," Caroline Denton, spokeswoman for LIFFE told Reuters.
"At the moment, our contract specification is based on a bond with a 12 percent coupon."

The Italian 7.75 percent 10-year bond was quoted with a yield of 7.92 percent at 1639 GMT. The yield has fallen sharply over the past year on speculation Italy may be ready to join EMU in the first wave in 1999.
